issues.description: The concept is the HTTP POST /persons endpoint that creates a new Person. The problem statement explicitly refers to a server-side method named `createPerson` (problem_statement.md), while the provided solution implements this operation as `addPerson` (solution repository PersonResource.java). The client-side PersonController also uses `addPerson` for sending the POST request. The template PersonResource.java contains only a TODO and does not declare `createPerson`. This inconsistent identifier usage (`createPerson` vs `addPerson`) for the same conceptual operation can confuse students: they may look for a `createPerson` stub to implement (as instructed) but find `addPerson` in the solution and client, increasing cognitive load and risking mismapping requirements to code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across all artifacts. Preferred minimal fix: update the problem statement to refer to `addPerson` (instead of `createPerson`) for the POST /persons endpoint so it matches the client (PersonController.addPerson) and the solution (PersonResource.addPerson). Alternative: rename the server method in the template and solution from `addPerson` to `createPerson` and update the client accordingly. Ensure all references in the problem text, template stubs, and solution use the same method name.
